name: GPS, GIS & Precision Agriculture

objectives.text: Describe how a GPS receiver determines a field location using signals from multiple satellites
Locate points on a farm map or GPS display using latitude and longitude coordinates
Explain the difference between a GPS point location and a GIS map layer showing field data
Identify common precision agriculture tools such as GPS guidance, auto-steer, yield monitors, and variable-rate controllers and the job each performs
Demonstrate the use of a GPS device to record field boundaries and calculate acreage
Compare GPS correction sources such as WAAS, subscription satellite correction, and RTK by accuracy, cost, and suitable field tasks
Explain how GPS guidance and auto-steer reduce overlap, skips, operator fatigue, and input waste in field operations
Analyze a GIS-generated yield map to identify variation in field productivity and suggest likely causes
Use GPS and GIS records to map and document a crop or land-based SAE enterprise
Build a multi-layer GIS map of a field combining boundaries, soil types, topography, and yield data
Explain how automatic section control and machine telematics use GPS position to manage implements and fleet data
Explain how georeferenced grid and zone soil sampling support site-specific nutrient management
Delineate management zones within a field by analyzing soil, yield, and elevation layers in GIS
Create a variable-rate seeding or fertilizer prescription map for the management zones of a field
Calibrate, install, and troubleshoot a GPS receiver, yield monitor, or variable-rate controller on farm equipment
Analyze results of a georeferenced on-farm strip trial to compare hybrids, varieties, or input rates
Analyze the natural resources of a farm or watershed with GIS to plan conservation practices such as buffer strips, waterways, and protection of erosion-prone areas
Evaluate the return on investment of a precision agriculture technology for a given farm operation
Evaluate how precision agriculture practices align with USDA sustainable practices criteria and affect stewardship of soil, water, and inputs
Evaluate questions of farm data ownership, privacy, and sharing when precision agriculture data is stored with equipment dealers or cloud platforms
Design a complete precision agriculture plan for an SAE plot or farm that integrates GPS guidance, GIS analysis, prescriptions, and economic justification

changes: Kept all six existing objectives, rewording the yield map objective to add likely causes. Replaced the generic variable-rate objective with a sequence: georeferenced soil sampling (10), management zone delineation (10), and a created prescription map (11). Added coordinate reading (6), identifying precision ag tools (7), GPS correction sources (9), guidance and auto-steer (9), GPS and GIS records for SAE (9), multi-layer GIS map building (10), section control and telematics (10), equipment calibration and troubleshooting (11), on-farm strip trial analysis (11), and GIS conservation planning (11). At grade 12 added sustainability alignment, farm data ownership, and a capstone SAE precision plan. Left surveying, drone, sensor, and emerging technology content to the sibling sub-topics. Standards are assigned only at grades 9 to 12.
